entries.claim: A function is denoted by one of the symbols f, m, Q, ...; the function f from the set X to the set Y is written $f : X \to Y$ and read "f is a function from X to Y".
entries.quote: The function is denoted by one of the following symbols: f or m

entries.claim: If f is a function from X to itself, f is called a function on X.
entries.quote: If f is a function from X to itself, we say that f is a function on X.

entries.claim: If the ordered pair (x, y) belongs to the function, y is called the image of x by f, expressed as $f : x \mapsto y$ (read: the function f maps x to y) or $f(x) = y$ (read: f is a function where f(x) = y).

entries.claim: The set X is called the domain of the function f.
entries.quote: The set X is called the domain of the function f.

entries.claim: The set Y is called the codomain of the function f.
entries.quote: The set Y is called the codomain of the function f.

entries.claim: The range is a subset of the codomain of the function.
